{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Daniel "Dan" Fleisch''' is an American physicist who specializes in [[electromagnetics]] and [[space physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2009/feb/11/daniel-fleisch-amazon-replacement|title=Author flies to Canada to replace reader's faulty copy of his book|first=Alison|last=Flood|work=The Guardian |date=February 11, 2009}}</ref> He is a Professor Emeritus of Physics at [[Wittenberg University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springfieldnewssun.com/news/wittenberg-to-host-wittclipse-viewing-party-activities-for-solar-eclipse/EYOJ5K3MHFCAHC5DHLNX66TZZE/|title=Wittenberg to host WittClipse viewing party for campus, activities for solar eclipse|website=springfield-news-sun}}</ref>

A minor planet is named after him.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springfieldnewssun.com/news/wittenberg-professor-has-minor-planet-named-after-him/FLK4FB2DOBBM3IYDI3JVJCWU3U/|title=Wittenberg professor has minor planet named after him|website=springfield-news-sun}}</ref>

==Biography==
Fleisch earned his B.S. from [[Georgetown University]] and his M.S. and Ph.D. from [[Rice University]] in [[space physics]] and [[astronomy]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.wittenberg.edu/academics/physics/facultystaff/fleisch.html|title=Daniel Fleisch, Ph.D. &#124; Wittenberg University|website=www.wittenberg.edu}}</ref> He has been a professor at [[Wittenberg University]] since 1998.<ref name="auto"/>

Fleisch has provided science commentary for [[PBS]] station [[WYSO]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wyso.org/community-calendar/event/the-planets-with-the-springfield-symphony-orchestra-05-10-2023-12-39-48|title=The Planets with the Springfield Symphony Orchestra|website=WYSO}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wyso.org/show/wyso-weekend/2012-02-19/springfield-symphony-goes-out-of-this-world-with-the-planets|title=Springfield Symphony Goes Out of This World With The Planets|website=WYSO}}</ref> and in 2006, appeared in the documentary ''The Dayton Codebreakers''.<ref name="auto"/>

==Writing==
Fleisch has authored several textbooks, including ''A Student's Guide to Maxwell's Equations''<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.cambridge.org/highereducation/books/a-students-guide-to-maxwells-equations/CB8D80B70E695AB8553D1F1117085AE3|title=A Student's Guide to Maxwell's Equations|first=Daniel|last=Fleisch|date=January 10, 2008|website=Higher Education from Cambridge University Press |doi=10.1017/CBO9780511984624 |isbn=978-0-521-87761-9 }}</ref> (2008) and ''A Student's Guide to Vectors and Tensors'' (2011).<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00107514.2012.739651|title=Scope: textbook. Level: pre-university, undergraduates, teachers, scientists, engineers|first=Peter R.|last=Hobson|date=November 1, 2012|via=Taylor and Francis+NEJM|doi=10.1080/00107514.2012.739651|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/zamm.201190027|title=Book Review: Daniel Fleisch, A Student's Guide to Vectors and Tensors, Cambridge University Press, Cambridge 2011|first=Holm|last=Altenbach|date=January 14, 2012|journal=ZAMM - Journal of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics / Zeitschrift für Angewandte Mathematik und Mechanik|volume=92|issue=1|pages=40|via=Wiley Online Library|doi=10.1002/zamm.201190027|bibcode=2012ZaMM...92...40A |url-access=subscription}}</ref> His other works include ''A Student's Guide to the Mathematics of Astronomy'' and ''A Student's Guide to Waves'', published in 2013 and 2014, respectively. In 2020, he published ''A Student's Guide to the Schrödinger equation''.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/00107514.2020.1756917|title=A student's guide to the Schrödinger equation|first=B.|last=Ishak|date=October 1, 2020|journal=Contemporary Physics|volume=61 |issue=4 |page=298 |via=www.tandfonline.com|doi=10.1080/00107514.2020.1756917|url-access=subscription}}</ref> His work has been translated into multiple languages, including [[Japanese language|Japanese]], [[Korean language|Korean]], [[Chinese language|Chinese]], and [[Italian language|Italian]].<ref name="auto"/>
